## Objects, values and names


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
#(3)Objects, values and names
# <- is called assign operator. Left is object name and right is value 
# data flows flows from right → left

## create an object (e.g., any vector) and assign it any name
x<-c(1,2,3,4)
y<-x  #this does not create new object (i.e., vector (1,2,3,4)), only get another binding y

#check the adress of object
lobstr::obj_addr(x)
lobstr::obj_addr(y)

#not a valid name
_a <- 5

#can use "" or ''
"_a"<-5
'_b'<-5

#Question: comment on a,b,c and d (are these different objects)
a <- 1:10
b <- a
c <- b
d <- 1:10
#check
list_1 <- list(a, b, c, d)
obj_addrs(list_1) #without calling the package "lobstr"


##copy-on-modify (modify some value in y)
y[[3]] <- 5 #change the third one
y[[5]]<- 6 #add new one
#now these are two different objects
obj_addr(x)
obj_addr(y)

#list and copy-on-modify with list command
list_2<-list(1,2,3,4)
list_3<-list_2
obj_addr(list_2)
obj_addr(list_3)

#modify list_3
list_3[[4]]<-5
list_3[[5]]<-6
obj_addr(list_2)
obj_addr(list_3)
```
:::


Two names can point to one object; R copies it only when one of them is modified (copy-on-modify).

## For loops


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
###Loops###

#A loop repeats the same task multiple times
#same task again and again
x1 <- 1^2
x2 <- 2^2
x3 <- 3^2

#Main loops in R: (1)for (2)while (3)repeat loops
#For loop : 
#for(values in sequence){ 
code that will repeat for all vlaues
}

#for vector
for(i in 1:3){
  print(i^2)
}   #print will only show results

for(i in c(1,2,3)){
  print(i^2)
}

#to use the results we need to save results from for loop
for(i in c(1,2,3)){
  x<-(i^2)
}  #this will only consider last value i.e., 3

#gen empty vector of length 3 and then x[i] will gen i^2
x<-numeric(3)

for (i in 1:3) {
  x[i] <- i^2
}

#for existing vector
x<-c(3,2,5)
for(i in x){print(i^2)
}

#this will overwrite x
for(i in x){x[i]<-(i^2)
}

#to store the loop results for x in y
y<-numeric(3)

for (i in x) {y[i]<-i^2}

#how to solve the issue
x <- c(3, 2, 5)
y <- numeric(length(x))

for (i in 1:length(x)) {
  y[i] <- (x[i])^2
}

for (i in 1:length(x)) {
  y[i] <- f(i)
}

y

#we can have more than one repeating codes
for(i in x){print(c(i,i^2,i^3))
}

for(i in x){z<-i^2
print(c(i,z))}

#write for loop and print z as x-mean(x)/sd(x)
```

Repeating a task, and saving the result in a vector.

## While and repeat loops


## The map family

```{.r .cell-code}

df1|>select(ID11,ID13,FM1,ID18C)|>export("data\\auxiliary_data\\hhd_1.dta")
#import this small file
df2<-import("data\\auxiliary_data\\hhd_1.dta")

## With out questionnaire check var details
install.packages("labelled")
library(labelled)
var_label(df2$ID11)
#change existing var labels
var_label(df2$ID11) <- "religion of houesehold head"

##rename req vars
df2<-df2|>rename(land=FM1,religion=ID11,education=ID18C)

##clean the data for vars
unique(education)
table(education)
attributes(education)
df2|>count(education) #preferable way

#let 16 years of educ is outlier (replace by NA)
df2 <- df2 |>mutate(education=na_if(education,16))
#or
df2<-df2|>mutate(education=ifelse(education==16,NA,education))


#create dummy from continuous variables
df2<-df2|>mutate(any_educ=ifelse(education>0,1,0|is.na(education)))
#add label for this now
var_label(df2$any_educ)<-"if any years of education"

#categories of education (1,2,3)
df2<- df2 |> 
  mutate(educ_cat= case_when(
    education <=5 ~ 1,
    education >5  & education <= 12 ~ 2,
    education >12 ~ 3
  ))

val_labels(df2$educ_cat) <- c(
  Primary = 1,
  High = 2,
  Higher = 3
)

#now begin analysis on hhd_2 data

######Data Analysis######
```

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data,aes(x=var1,y=var2))+
  geom_yourchoice()

##bar chat [total count to begin with]
ggplot(df2, aes(x = educ_cat)) +
  geom_bar()  #will not include NAs and will consider x as continuous

ggplot(df2, aes(x = factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_bar()  #will include NAs and will consider x as categorical

ggplot(df2, aes(x = factor(educ_cat), fill=factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_bar()  #add legend and colors

ggplot(df2|>filter(!is.na(educ_cat)), aes(x = factor(educ_cat, levels=c(1,2,3),labels=c("Low","high","higher")), fill=factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_bar()  #get rid of NAs

#this will remove legend
ggplot(df2|>filter(!is.na(educ_cat)), aes(x = factor(educ_cat,levels=c(1,2,3),labels=c("Low","High","Higher")), fill = factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_bar()

ggplot(df2|>filter(!is.na(educ_cat)), aes(x = factor(educ_cat,levels=c(1,2,3),labels=c("Low","High","Higher")), fill = factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_bar() + theme(legend.position = "none")

#edit axis labels and titles: labs()
ggplot(df2|>filter(!is.na(educ_cat)), aes(x = factor(educ_cat,levels=c(1,2,3),labels=c("Low","High","Higher")), fill = factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_bar() + labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Bar Plot",
    x = "Education Category",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Educ cat"
  ) + theme(legend.position = "none") + theme_minimal() + theme()

#over all theme and position of title and legend
ggplot(df2|>filter(!is.na(educ_cat)), aes(x = factor(educ_cat,levels=c(1,2,3),labels=c("Low","High","Higher")), fill = factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_bar() + labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Bar Plot",
    x = "Education Category",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Educ cat"
  ) +  theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
                               legend.position = "")


#Now let's do proportions
df2|>filter(!is.na(educ_cat))|>
  count(educ_cat)|>mutate(prop=n/sum(n))|>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(educ_cat,levels=c(1,2,3),
                        labels=c("Low","High","Higher")), y=prop, fill = factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_col() + labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Bar Plot",
    x = "Education Category",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Educ cat"
  ) +  theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
                               legend.position = "")


install.packages("scales")
library(scales)

#convert y label into %
df2|>filter(!is.na(educ_cat))|>
  count(educ_cat)|>mutate(prop=n/sum(n))|>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(educ_cat,levels=c(1,2,3),
                        labels=c("Low","High","Higher")), y=prop, fill = factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_col() + scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) + labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Bar Plot",
    x = "Education Category",
    y = "Percent",
    fill = "Educ cat"
  ) +  theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
                               legend.position = "")

#add percent at top of bar (by geom_text)
df2|>filter(!is.na(educ_cat))|>
  count(educ_cat)|>mutate(prop=n/sum(n),top_lab=paste0(round(prop*100,1),"%"))|>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(educ_cat,levels=c(1,2,3),
                        labels=c("Low","High","Higher")), y=prop, fill = factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_col() + scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) + 
  geom_text(
    aes(label = top_lab),
    vjust = -0.05,   # moves text above bars
    size = 2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Bar Plot",
    x = "Education Category",
    y = "Percent",
    fill = "Educ cat"
  ) +  theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
                               legend.position = "")


#Side by side
df2|>filter(!is.na(educ_cat),!is.na(land))|>
  count(educ_cat,land) |> mutate(prop=n/sum(n))|>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(educ_cat,levels=c(1,2,3),
                        labels=c("Low","High","Higher")), y=prop, fill = factor(land,levels=c(0,1),
                                                                                labels=c("No","Yes")))) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") + scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) + labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Bar Plot",
    x = "Education Category",
    y = "Percent",
    fill = "Land"
  ) +  theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
                               legend.position = "right")
```

## Pie chart


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
#prepare a pie chart for "educ_cat" (title, legend and percentages(outside the slices) should be there)
#simple pie chart
df2|>
  filter(!is.na(educ_cat))|>
  count(educ_cat)|>
  mutate(
    prop = n / sum(n)
  )|>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = prop, fill = factor(educ_cat))) +
  geom_col() + coord_polar(theta = "y") +  theme_void()

#final pie chart
df2|>
  filter(!is.na(educ_cat))|>
  count(educ_cat)|>
  mutate(
    prop = n / sum(n),
    values = paste0(round(prop * 100, 1),"%")
  )|>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = prop, fill = factor(educ_cat,levels=c(1,2,3),
                                             labels=c("Low","High","Higher")))) +
  geom_col() + coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = values),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 2
  ) + theme_void() + labs(fill = "Educ Cat")
```
:::


Simple and final version with labels.

```{.r .cell-code}
  ggplot(aes(y=COPC)) + geom_boxplot(fill="orange") +  
  labs(title="Box Plot 1", y="Consumption")

sum(df2$COPC > 30000, na.rm = TRUE) #how many obs of COPC are >50000

#histogram
ggplot(df2, aes(education, fill="red")) + geom_histogram(bins=8) +
  labs(title="hist_1", x="Education Years", y="Count") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0,4,8,12,16)) + labs(fill = "Educ") + 
  theme(legend.position = "")
```
